newsitem.title: CYPRUS: British bases in Cyprus release teenager.
newsitem.headline: British bases in Cyprus release teenager.

text.p: British military bases authorities in Cyprus on Thursday released a Greek teenager jailed for traffic offences after granting him clemency, a base statement said.
The imprisonment of George Kyriakos for three months sparked protests on Sunday by anti-bases campaigners outside his jail in Dhekelia, one of two British sovereign bases on the island.
But the British bases authorities said the protests had no bearing on their decision to release Kyriakos two months early.

An appeal for clemency had been granted by the bases administrator, Air Vice-Marshal Peter Millar, after considering a social welfare report and Kyriakos's exemplary behaviour while in custody, the statement added.
Kyriakos, 17, was jailed for a string of motoring offences committed in areas controlled by the British military bases. Britain has retained two bases in Cyprus since independence in 1960.
A police force is empowered to prosecute any offender within bases territory. Many Cypriots do not recognise the authority of the British bases in passing judgement on them.
Around 50 protestors demanding the release of Kyriakos hurled stones at the police station of Dhekelia base in south eastern Cyprus on Sunday and burnt tyres.
